purpose: Declared-failure ledger for `python scripts/check_forecast_invariants.py --sidecar-dir` (CI job `forecast-invariant-artifacts`, added by FFR-1D for audit finding FR-24). Every FAIL recorded in a committed run sidecar under frontend/data/hindcast/ must appear here, so a NEWLY registered run that fails an invariant is a reviewed line in this file rather than a number that lands on the forecast dashboard unremarked. Adding a line is not absolution: an invariant FAIL is a root-cause finding (rules 1/11), and the open ones are tracked in docs/forecast-readiness-audit-2026-07.md.
how_to_update: Registering a run whose sidecar carries a FAIL: add `"<run_id>": ["I4", ...]` below in the same commit as the registration, and name the finding it belongs to in your findings doc. Removing a run's sidecar, or fixing the defect so the invariant passes, means DELETING its line here — the checker fails on a stale declaration too.

ffr2b_note: FFR-2B (2026-08-02) declared five previously-undeclared runs, in the commit that repairs this job. FOUR ARE FFR-2B'S OWN and were the session's own miss — the runs were registered without their line here: miso-2021-2025-cmc-{legacy,pipeline}-ffr2b carry I9 (storage simultaneity, 0.36/0.56 % of throughput, BIT-IDENTICAL across the two arms and therefore not attributable to retirement_rule); miso-2026-2030-ffr2b-t1f-base carries I7 and -dampers carries I7 + I12. The T1-F pair's I7/I12 are the SUBSTANTIVE D-2 finding, not noise: arming entry_rate_limits + entry_commissioning_lag widens I7 from one failing year (2026) to three (2026-2028) and pushes I12 from WARN to FAIL, because the damped arm stops concealing an adequacy shortfall the base arm closed with an unbuildable 4.9 GW single-year gas_ct wave (MISO's actual 2021-25 gas_ct additions totalled 1.379 GW). Recorded as a disclosed cost of owner decision D-2, not tuned away (rule 1) — docs/handoffs/ffr-2b-retirement-entry-evidence-2026-08-02.md §1.3/§3. THE FIFTH IS NOT FFR-2B'S: ercot-2023-2025-t1ff-armr-fh1gate (I6, I7) is FH-1's §3.3 harness-defect gate probe, registered earlier the same day without a declaration, which left this CI job RED ON MAIN before FFR-2B merged. post_clear_note: 2026-08-19: first post-clear registration. pjm-2021-2025-realized-k162 (T1-H plain hindcast 2021-2025 on the current PJM keeper 2026-08-15-pjm-162-inputclock) carries I7 — 2025 accredited firm 138,785 MW vs a 139,850 MW requirement, a 1,065 MW / 0.76 % shortfall. THIS IS NOT THE FR-3 HYDRO CAUSE listed in dominant_open_causes: PJM hydro IS accredited in this run (firm_clean_accredited_mw 1,254 MW of 3,301 MW LP nameplate). The cause is upstream, in the retirement ledger, and it is the harness working as designed rather than a defect. The 2022 bridge-year evolution retires 4,097 MW of nuclear on reason='announced' — Byron 1+2 (plant 6023) and Dresden 2+3 (plant 869), whose 2020-vintage EIA-860 rows carry Exelon's 2020-08-27 PJM deactivation dates. Illinois CEJA (P.A. 102-0662) reversed both on 2021-09-15, so PJM actually retired 0 GW of nuclear in the window; but the RC-1B information gate in data.confirmed_retirements.load_announced_reversal_plants keys the reversal on superseding_instrument_date (2021-09-15) against this run's 2020-12-31 vintage cutoff, and therefore correctly declines to suppress the announced exit — its own docstring names this exact case. A forecaster standing at end-2020 would have retired both plants. That 4,097 MW of removed firm nuclear is ~3.8x the I7 shortfall and is also 62 % of the run's 6.645 GW false-retire total, so the I7 FAIL, the false-retire FAIL and the +13 % thermal-retire band miss share this one cause. Declared, NOT absolution, and no band or threshold was touched (rules 1/11/14).
